items.title: SpaceX to launch 15th Starship flight, seeking to achieve unprecedented round trip - Reuters
items.snippet: SpaceX to launch 15th Starship flight, seeking to achieve unprecedented round trip Reuters
items.summary: A Reuters report by Joey Roulette, published 13 November 2026, says SpaceX’s 15th Starship flight was scheduled to lift off at 4:45 p.m. CT from Starbase and will try for the first time to catch the upper stage at the Texas launch site rather than ditching it in the ocean, after also returning the Super Heavy booster — a mission that would also be the rocket’s second to deploy operational Starlink satellites. SpaceX secured its FAA launch license hours before the planned liftoff; if the plan holds, the booster would be caught and then moved off the pad so the ship can return after about 22 hours and 14 orbits, with the debut ship catch around 2:45 p.m. CT on Saturday.

items.title: SpaceX faces key launch test tonight with 'double catch' of Starship and Super Heavy Booster - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: SpaceX faces key launch test tonight with 'double catch' of Starship and Super Heavy Booster Yahoo Finance
items.summary: A Yahoo Finance article by Pras Subramanian, published 13 November 2026, says SpaceX’s Starship Flight 15 is scheduled for Friday night at 5:45 p.m. ET and will attempt a first-time “double catch” of both the Super Heavy booster and the Starship upper stage at Boca Chica, which the company said would be the first full recovery of an orbital launch system, while also deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites that SpaceX says add 1 terabit of capacity each — about equal to ten Falcon 9 V2 Mini launches. Morgan Stanley’s Adam Jonas called the flight “one of the most significant catalysts in SpaceX’s 20+ year history”; the piece notes the stock was up 2% for the week after trading between $148.44 and $135.40, and cites Bloomberg reporting that a SpaceX–Tesla merger could be announced as early as December or slip into early 2027.

items.title: SpaceX’s Starship Launch Today Could Lift the Stock - Barron's
items.snippet: SpaceX’s Starship Launch Today Could Lift the Stock Barron's
items.summary: A Barron’s article by Al Root, published 13 November 2026, says SpaceX is scheduled to launch the 15th Starship test on Friday evening, aiming for a first-ever double catch of both the Super Heavy booster and the upper stage with the launch tower’s mechanical arms, after the stock had been down about 4% coming into Friday trading since the 14th test on 28 September 2026. The rest of the article is paywalled; Barron’s own bullet summary on the page says the company hopes to have Starship fully operational by late 2027 to deploy AI data-center satellites and next-generation Starlink satellites.

items.title: Double-catch drama: Why Starship's Flight 15 is so important to SpaceX - Space
items.snippet: Double-catch drama: Why Starship's Flight 15 is so important to SpaceX Space
items.summary: A Space.com article by Andrew Jones, published 13 November 2026, says SpaceX is targeting today for Starship Flight 15 — the first attempt to catch the Ship upper stage as well as the Super Heavy booster, which the company calls the “Holy Grail of rocketry” — with a 75-minute window opening at 5:45 p.m. EST, a first catch of a next-gen Super Heavy V3 about 6.5 minutes after liftoff, and, if conditions are met, a Ship catch back at Starbase about 21 hours later after deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites. Jones writes that a successful double catch would be the first full recovery of an orbital launch system, a step toward the roughly 10,000 Starship launches a year SpaceX is targeting by 2030, and quotes Elon Musk saying that if both catches succeed it will mark the first time all parts of an orbital rocket return to Earth intact — “the critical breakthrough needed to make life multiplanetary.”

items.title: SpaceX's giant rocket may leave NASA in the dust - NPR
items.snippet: SpaceX's giant rocket may leave NASA in the dust NPR
items.summary: An NPR report by Geoff Brumfiel, published 13 November 2026, says SpaceX plans its most ambitious Starship test later today — lift off from South Texas, orbit Earth, and land vertically at the same pad 22 and a half hours later — and that experts warn the shift toward Starship could strand NASA, because SpaceX has said it will stop flying Falcon 9, which launches Dragon, currently the only American spacecraft that can ferry NASA astronauts to and from the ISS. NASA has contracted three additional ISS flights that would only take Dragon through 2028 if flown every six months with no further orders; SpaceX did not comment, its latest report showed about $2.1 billion of launch revenue through September versus $12.8 billion from Starlink and $10.9 billion from AI, and Gwynne Shotwell suggested Boeing’s problem-plagued Starliner (next crewed flight sometime in 2028) could take some of that NASA business.

items.title: 'Don't panic': SpaceX pens familiar message on Starship ahead of historic double-catch test flight - Space
items.snippet: 'Don't panic': SpaceX pens familiar message on Starship ahead of historic double-catch test flight Space
items.summary: A Space.com piece by Mike Wall, published 13 November 2026, notes that SpaceX rolled Ship 42 to the Starbase pad on 12 November with “Don’t panic” painted on the vehicle — a Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy nod that also plays on the ship’s number, 42 — ahead of Starship Flight 15’s first attempt to catch both stages on the tower’s chopstick arms. The 75-minute launch window opens at 5:45 p.m. EST; Super Heavy is due back about 6.5 minutes after liftoff, and Ship 42 is to deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites, circle Earth 14 times, and attempt its own catch on 14 November about 22.5 hours later, or splash down in the Pacific near Hawaii or Chile if a catch is called off.

items.title: United Airlines CEO: Starlink is our biggest competitive advantage in 100 years - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: United Airlines CEO: Starlink is our biggest competitive advantage in 100 years Yahoo Finance
items.summary: A Yahoo Finance piece by Brian Sozzi, dated 12 November 2026, quotes United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby at Yahoo Finance Invest calling Starlink Wi-Fi “the biggest near-term competitive advantage that we’ve ever had in United’s 100-year history,” the No. 1 reason people pick a flight, and a reason customers are trying United, with all JFK flights to be on Starlink when the airline starts service there. Jefferies’ Sheila Kahyaoglu said United has equipped nearly 600 aircraft (300 regional and 300 mainline); Kirby said 50% of the mainline fleet should have Starlink by year-end, 87% by the end of next summer, and 100% of the fleet by the end of 2027, called Amazon’s Leo “a mistake,” and said he still respects Delta, which has signed up for a Leo rollout not expected to begin until 2028.

items.title: SpaceX, Tesla merger talks progress, Bloomberg News reports - Reuters
items.snippet: SpaceX, Tesla merger talks progress, Bloomberg News reports Reuters
items.summary: A Reuters report dated 12 November 2026, citing Bloomberg News and people familiar with the matter, says SpaceX and Tesla are progressing in their merger negotiations and that a deal could be announced as early as December. The companies have also discussed a scenario in which the announcement slips into early 2027; Reuters said SpaceX and Tesla could not be immediately reached for comment. Reuters.com itself was paywalled here (401); this summary is from the same Reuters brief as carried by CNA.

items.title: SpaceX-Tesla Merger Could Come Soon: What Do Shareholders Get? - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: SpaceX-Tesla Merger Could Come Soon: What Do Shareholders Get? Yahoo Finance
items.summary: A BeInCrypto article by Lockridge Okoth, dated 12 November 2026 and listed in Google News under Yahoo Finance, says Bloomberg reported that SpaceX–Tesla merger talks are progressing and a deal could be announced as early as December, though no terms are signed and the timetable could slip into 2027. It cites Bank of America analyst Alexander Perry saying SpaceX would buy Tesla with stock, leaving Tesla holders with about 47% of the combined company at a 20% premium on 20 October prices, and notes Tesla’s majority-of-outstanding-shares vote rule plus China regulatory risk could still block the deal.

items.title: SpaceX plans over $74 billion investment in Texas, Arizona AI campuses - Reuters
items.snippet: SpaceX plans over $74 billion investment in Texas, Arizona AI campuses Reuters
items.summary: A Reuters report dated 12 November 2026 says SpaceX plans to invest more than $74 billion in two supercomputing campuses — more than $24 billion at Starbase in Texas and roughly $50 billion in Cochise County, Arizona — expanding an AI business that already generated more than half of third-quarter revenue. The Arizona campus still needs county approval and faces a 2,400-signature petition ahead of a December public hearing, while a Starbase city notice describes a gas-fired power plant and supercomputing facility on about 444 acres, with the City Commission due to consider a property tax abatement on 9 December.

items.title: SpaceX and Tesla Talks on Record Merger Are Said to Progress - Bloomberg.com
items.snippet: SpaceX and Tesla Talks on Record Merger Are Said to Progress Bloomberg.com
items.summary: A Bloomberg report dated 12 November 2026, by Ryan Gould, Siddharth Philip and Dinesh Nair, citing people familiar with the matter, says SpaceX and Tesla are advancing merger talks and could announce a deal as early as December, though the companies have also considered slipping that announcement into early 2027. Boards and advisers are working through terms and the combined company’s governance; sources flagged isolating Tesla’s China operations from SpaceX’s U.S. government and defense work as a hurdle, and neither company immediately commented. Bloomberg.com itself was not directly reachable here; this summary is from the same Bloomberg article as carried by Bloomberg Línea.

items.title: SpaceX Plans $74 Billion Investment to Build Data Centers in Texas and Arizona - The New York Times
items.snippet: SpaceX Plans $74 Billion Investment to Build Data Centers in Texas and Arizona The New York Times
items.summary: A New York Times report dated 12 November 2026 says SpaceX plans a $74 billion investment to build data centers in Texas and Arizona. That tracks SpaceX’s own 12 November update, which puts more than $24 billion into a self-powered supercompute site at Starbase in the Rio Grande Valley and about $50 billion into a Cochise County, Arizona campus; the NYT page itself did not return a readable full text here, so this summary is from the headline plus that official company update.

items.title: SpaceX’s next move is chasing the unprecedented ‘holy grail’ of rocketry. Here’s what’s at stake - CNN
items.snippet: SpaceX’s next move is chasing the unprecedented ‘holy grail’ of rocketry. Here’s what’s at stake CNN
items.summary: A CNN report by Jackie Wattles, dated 12 November 2026, says SpaceX will try on Friday, in a window from 5:45 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. ET, to bring both stages of Starship back intact — the first attempt at full recovery of an orbital launch system, which the company has called the “holy grail” of rocketry. The piece notes that a Super Heavy V3 booster has not yet been caught, that catching the roughly 52-metre Ship from orbit in the tower arms has never been demonstrated, and that FAA rules require showing the chance of a casualty is below 1 in 1 million. CNN.com English did not return a usable page here; this is from CNN’s Spanish edition of the same Wattles article.

items.title: Building the future — Starbase and Cochise County supercompute investments
items.summary: SpaceX’s 12 November 2026 Updates post says it is advancing two supercompute projects — a facility at Starbase in the Rio Grande Valley and a campus in Cochise County, Arizona — that together represent more than $74 billion in planned U.S. investment. It plans more than $24 billion of new supercomputing at Starbase (on top of more than $15 billion already invested there), with the site generating its own power, plus $220 million to expand Brownsville’s water and wastewater capacity by 20 million gallons a day, and a roughly $50 billion Arizona campus expected to support about 5,500 construction jobs and 1,000 permanent jobs, using dry cooling with no planned industrial groundwater use.
items.timeSource: Official SpaceX posts linking the 12 November Updates item

items.title: Not Starlink. Not Starship. This Is the Real Reason SpaceX Stock Could Soar Before 2027 Arrives. - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: Not Starlink. Not Starship. This Is the Real Reason SpaceX Stock Could Soar Before 2027 Arrives. Yahoo Finance
items.summary: A Motley Fool column by Keithen Drury, dated 12 Nov 2026 and listed in this feed as Yahoo Finance, argues that Super Intelligence — not Starlink or Starship — is the real reason SPCX could rally before 2027, noting SI revenue grew 830% year over year to $7.56 billion in Q3, more than half of SpaceX’s $14.6 billion total. He cites Musk’s view that annual recurring revenue could reach $500 billion to $1 trillion by the end of 2027, while warning that the stock could struggle if the market stays bearish on heavy AI spending.

items.title: Dear SpaceX Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 13 - Barchart.com
items.snippet: Dear SpaceX Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 13 Barchart.com
items.summary: A Barchart column by Ebube Jones, published 12 Nov 2026, tells SPCX holders to mark Friday 13 Nov for Starship Flight 15, when SpaceX plans to catch both the Super Heavy booster and the Starship upper stage with the launch tower’s mechanical arms — a first if it succeeds — after Flight 14 reached orbit on 28 Sept and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites. Jones notes shares have fallen almost 12% over the past month and that SpaceX and Tesla lost about $456 billion in combined market value after the midterms, argues a successful double catch could help the stock bounce back but would not erase valuation or spending concerns, and cites Morgan Stanley’s Adam Jonas at Overweight with a $300 price target plus a 40-analyst “Moderate Buy” consensus averaging $252.05.

items.title: Ukraine warns of fresh Starshield disruptions as U.S. envoys arrive in Moscow for talks with Putin - CNBC
items.snippet: Ukraine warns of fresh Starshield disruptions as U.S. envoys arrive in Moscow for talks with Putin CNBC
items.summary: A CNBC report dated 12 November 2026 says President Volodymyr Zelenskyy alleged fresh, systematic speed restrictions on SpaceX’s Starshield service over Ukraine, with terminals disconnecting above 161 km/h (100 mph) and making it harder to intercept Russian jet-powered drones along the front line and in occupied territories. CNBC says it reached out to SpaceX and the White House for comment, notes similar limits were imposed in mid-October and lifted by 24 October, and places Zelenskyy’s remarks as U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow for talks with Vladimir Putin.

items.title: Prediction: $1,000 Invested in SpaceX Today Will Be Worth This Much by 2029 - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: Prediction: $1,000 Invested in SpaceX Today Will Be Worth This Much by 2029 Yahoo Finance
items.summary: A Motley Fool column by Rick Orford, dated 12 November 2026 and carried by Yahoo Finance, sketches three earnings-based scenarios for what $1,000 in SPCX could be worth by 2029, citing Q3 revenue of $14.6 billion, $4.4 billion of net income, 13.6 million Starlink subscribers and about $19.6 billion of capex. Its conservative case (30% annual sales growth, a 20 times price-to-sales multiple) implies about $810; the base case (45%, 25 times) about $1,400; and the optimistic case (60%, 30 times) about $2,260 — the author’s calculations, not a company forecast.

items.title: USSF-627 mission
items.summary: SpaceX’s official USSF-627 page now confirms that Falcon 9 lifted off at 8:36 p.m. PT on 11 November 2026 from Space Launch Complex 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base. It says this was the seventh flight for the first-stage booster, which had previously launched NROL-179, SDA-T1TL-E, SDA-T1TL-A and three Starlink missions, and that after stage separation the booster landed on the Of Course I Still Love You droneship in the Pacific Ocean.

items.snippet: Stock Market Today, Nov. 11: SpaceX Shares Slip Amid Upcoming Starship Test Flight Jitters Yahoo Finance

He also flags the 8 December lock-up expiry and notes Q3 revenue of $14.6 billion, up 161%, including $7.6 billion from the AI business; volume was about 111 million shares, and the stock is down 13% since the 2026 IPO.

items.summary: A Motley Fool column by Johnny Rice, dated 11 Nov 2026 and listed in this feed as Yahoo Finance, treats Friday’s Starship Flight 15 as a major event for SPCX and quotes Morgan Stanley’s Adam Jonas calling a successful catch potentially “the biggest positive catalyst since the IPO.” SpaceX plans to catch both the Super Heavy booster and, for the first time, the Starship upper stage at Starbase after a window opening around 5:45 p.m. ET, then fly more than 22 hours, complete about 14 orbits and deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites before a Saturday catch attempt; the author notes that none of the latest V3 boosters have been caught yet and that a miss could push the payoff further out.

items.title: Google's SpaceX investment takes an unexpected turn - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: Google's SpaceX investment takes an unexpected turn Yahoo Finance
items.summary: A TheStreet column by Hillary Remy and Dana Sullivan Kilroy, dated 10 Nov 2026 and listed in this feed as Yahoo Finance, says Alphabet raised its SpaceX holding to about 555 million shares, up from 551.2 million, while paying SpaceX $920 million a month for xAI data-center capacity from October 2026 through June 2029 — a contract TheStreet puts at roughly $30 billion, covering about 110,000 Nvidia GPUs. The piece notes Alphabet booked an $8.7 billion third-quarter equity-securities loss driven mainly by the SpaceX share drop, that Google called the GPU arrangement bridge capacity for Gemini (either side can exit with 90 days’ notice after 2026), and that Google executive Don Harrison has resigned from SpaceX’s board.

items.title: Prediction: Here's How Much SpaceX Will Be Worth by the End of 2027 - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: Prediction: Here's How Much SpaceX Will Be Worth by the End of 2027 Yahoo Finance
items.summary: A Motley Fool column by Justin Pope, dated 10 November 2026 and carried on Yahoo Finance, predicts SPCX could finish 2027 around $250, about 65% above the then-current $134, after a $1.77 trillion IPO and a pullback to roughly the $135 offer price. The piece cites Q3 Super Intelligence revenue of $7.56 billion and Connectivity revenue of $5.25 billion with 13.6 million subscribers, and reaches that $250 target by annualizing the high end of Q1 2027 guidance to about $150 billion of 2027 revenue and applying a 20 times sales multiple, while warning of political and AI-industry risks.

items.title: SpaceX - Britannica
items.snippet: SpaceX Britannica
items.summary: The Google News link and the main Britannica page were blocked; Britannica’s Scholars encyclopedia entry by Alison Eldridge describes SpaceX as an American aerospace company founded by Elon Musk in 2002, now headquartered in Starbase, Texas, and covers Falcon, Dragon, Starlink and Starship plus the February 2026 xAI acquisition, a June 2026 IPO of 555.6 million shares at $135 that raised $75 billion and valued the company at about $1.77 trillion, and the August 2026 $60 billion purchase of Cursor. It says that as of June 2026 Starlink had more than 10,200 satellites in orbit and 12 million subscribers, and that after the xAI deal SpaceX made artificial intelligence one of its three main business segments alongside space and connectivity.

items.title: 8-K — Item 8.01, Apollo GPU finance-lease commitment
items.summary: The 8-K says that on 24 Oct 2026 SpaceX signed a binding commitment for a master finance lease with an Apollo-managed lessor that will buy GPU pods and related equipment and lease them to SpaceX. The company expects about $40 billion of principal payments over roughly five-year tranche schedules, with closing targeted by year-end 2026 and deliveries in the first half of 2027; an IR release adds that the chips are next-generation NVIDIA Vera Rubin GPUs and that Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, and KKR also committed.

items.summary: An 8-K says SpaceX closed its acquisition of Anysphere (Cursor) on 14 Aug 2026, converting outstanding Cursor stock into 389,289,254 SpaceX Class A shares at an implied $60 billion equity value, plus 1,752,426 shares for vested RSUs before tax withholding.
